core_obligations: Translate the diagram (proof lines 5387-5400): an object of the fibre category of the 2-fibre product over A is a triple (u, v, a) with a morphism a from f(u) to g(v); a diagram over A_1 -> A with A_2 -> A surjective becomes a diagram of such triples with components in the three categories.

Build the candidate fibre product (proof lines 5400-5424): by (RS) for the two outer categories there are fibre products u_1 x_u u_2 and v_1 x_v v_2 over A_1 x_A A_2, and by (RS) for the middle category together with the fibre square lemma, the images of these fibre products under f and g are fibre squares in the middle category; hence the comparison morphism a_1 x_a a_2 can be viewed as a morphism from f(u_1 x_u u_2) to g(v_1 x_v v_2) over A_1 x_A A_2.

Conclude (proof lines 5424-5438): the triple formed by the two fibre products and the comparison morphism makes the displayed square a fibre square in the 2-fibre product, which is precisely (RS) for the 2-fibre product.
proof_roadmap: Translate objects and diagrams of the 2-fibre product into triples.
Apply (RS) in the two outer categories and use the fibre square lemma in the middle one to combine the comparison morphisms.
Assemble the fibre square and read off (RS).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that if three categories cofibred in groupoids appearing in a 2-fibre product square all satisfy (RS), then the 2-fibre product satisfies (RS) (statement lines 5371-5385). The proof (proof lines 5387-5441) translates a diagram in the 2-fibre product into triples, builds the candidate fibre product from the fibre products in the two outer categories and the comparison morphism moved along the fibre squares in the middle category, and verifies the fibre square condition.
